data.description:
`rebar review-code --ref <sha> --source attested` accepts both values, forwards them through the
library, and drops them at the shim. This is not merely unimplemented: `CodeReviewRequest` has a
`source` field (`gate_dispatch.py:297`) that `gate_source.resolve_gate_handle` consumes
(`gate_dispatch.py:433`), so the caller's request is actively discarded at the seam.

`llm/code_review/shim.py:127-128` declares `ref`/`source`; the `CodeReviewRequest(...)` literal at
`:146-158` omits them. `shim.py` never imports `gate_source`, and `_verdict_to_review_result`
(`:79-104`) never stamps `source`/`verified_at_sha` — while `operations.py:242`,
`completion.py:488`, `plan_review/__init__.py:473` and `spec_scan.py:69` all do.

`_mcp_llm.py:93-96` tells MCP callers that results carry `source`/`verified_at_sha`/`signable`.
That is a false promise on the trust boundary that decides whether a code review can be signed:
`--source attested` silently reviews the dirty working tree and yields an unsignable result,
indistinguishable from a successful attested run.

Highest-scoring finding of the audit (validity 1.0, impact 0.92). Both remediation proposers
converged on this approach independently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ref` and `source` are forwarded into the `CodeReviewRequest` literal
- [ ] `_verdict_to_review_result` stamps `source` and `verified_at_sha`, matching the four sibling producers
- [ ] A behavioural test covers each `source` value, not just the signature change
- [ ] `_mcp_llm.py`'s documented promise is true of the returned result
data.title: Wire code-review provenance: --ref/--source are dropped at the shim
